ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether HBM-related probe-card demand is recurring, supply-constrained, and margin-accretive; verify DRAM/HBM mix, backlog, customer concentration, lead times, and whether revenue is tied to multiple HBM suppliers.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need filing-level proof that HBM probe-card revenue is material and recurring rather than a short-lived win.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Most direct hidden HBM-test exposure in the set, with a clear path through DRAM/HBM probe-card mix, backlog, and customer concentration. Test remains a gate before costly AI accelerator integration, so the bottleneck logic is strong and measurable.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Usually screened as a probe-card or semiconductor test name rather than an AI infrastructure supplier, so the HBM linkage can be missed unless you inspect segment mix and customer priorities.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Track AI-specific backlog, liquid-cooling adoption, margins, capacity, order conversion, and whether valuation already embeds bottleneck expectations.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need to separate fundamental bottleneck strength from market-pricing risk; the key question is not whether exposure exists, but how much is already discounted.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Vertiv has the strongest direct exposure to AI data-center power and thermal infrastructure, including high-density cooling and power systems. However, it is ranked below several underfollowed candidates in Serenity research priority because it is already a high-attention reference leader and may already reflect significant AI bottleneck expectations.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included as a benchmark for AI data-center power/cooling backlog, pricing, margins, and order conversion.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether the announced HBM inspection/metrology win converts into repeat production orders, broader customer adoption, and meaningful revenue contribution versus a niche platform sale.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that the HBM-related opportunity is recurring and material, not just a single design win.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Another direct gate on HBM and advanced-packaging test and inspection, with a relatively clean way to validate whether the AI linkage is real through orders, revenue mix, and utilization.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Typically labeled as cyclical back-end test equipment, not as an AI or HBM bottleneck candidate.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify data-center cooling revenue, liquid-cooling product mix, capacity, margins, customer concentration, and whether AI rack density is driving incremental demand.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-company evidence separating AI/data-center cooling from broader HVAC and industrial thermal revenue, plus proof of customer qualification or backlog tied to high-density AI deployments.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Modine ranks highest because liquid cooling and thermal management are direct rack-density constraints in AI infrastructure, while the company is still often classified as industrial HVAC/thermal management rather than as a core AI data-center supplier. The demand driver is durable if AI rack power density continues rising, and the thesis is testable through data-center revenue growth, cooling product mix, backlog, margins, capacity additions, and customer commentary.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Industrial thermal-management labeling can obscure data-center and liquid-cooling exposure, especially relative to more obvious AI infrastructure names such as Vertiv.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify AI data-center-related utility transmission demand, backlog mix, permitting constraints, labor constraints, and margin durability.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need more specific attribution of backlog and margin expansion to AI data-center grid demand versus broad grid hardening, renewables interconnection, and utility capex.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Quanta is a high-quality reference anchor for the grid-interconnection, transmission, and utility-infrastructure bottleneck. It ranks lower in the Serenity priority list because it is already widely recognized within infrastructure and has less underfollowed-discovery value than smaller or more obscure electrical-services candidates.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed within infrastructure, but less obvious than semiconductor names as an AI capacity bottleneck anchor.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify data-center orders, switchgear lead times, capacity additions, backlog, margin expansion, and whether AI-driven demand is already priced.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need to determine how much AI data-center power demand is incremental versus already reflected in consensus expectations and valuation.

It is strategically important to the theme but ranks last in this chunk for Serenity discovery because it is a mega-cap, high-attention name with limited underfollowed alpha value relative to smaller suppliers and services companies.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; it is included to benchmark electrical equipment demand, switchgear lead times, capacity, backlog, and margin signals.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify current InP revenue, customer concentration, capacity, yield, China-related operating risk, AI datacenter optical exposure, and whether demand is from AI-relevant transceivers or older telecom cycles.

ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Obscure small-cap substrate supplier hidden behind photonics and telecom labels, so it can be missed by investors focused only on branded optical module vendors.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify data-center project exposure, backlog, labor constraints, margins, project timing, and customer concentration.

If grid connection, electrical installation, switchgear integration, and data-center build execution become practical deployment bottlenecks, specialized contractors may capture durable demand despite being excluded from semiconductor-centric AI screens.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Services and contracting names can be missed because they do not sell GPUs, optical modules, branded cooling systems, or visible data-center equipment.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify actual HBM-adjacent production revenue, named AI accelerator customers, advanced-packaging capex, utilization, CHIPS Act-related capacity, and whether AI is material rather than marketing language.

ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Compared with TSMC and NVIDIA, the AI angle is embedded in OSAT and advanced packaging categories rather than obvious AI branding.

The name is less clean than pure optics leaders, but that dilution creates a potential discovery setup if data-center products become a larger revenue driver.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: AI infrastructure exposure may be diluted by IoT, analog, mixed-signal, and legacy connectivity segments, causing screens to miss specific optical/connectivity content.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify AI/data-center segment growth, customer concentration, margin durability, exposure to networking or accelerator systems, and working-capital requirements.

ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is not a branded AI platform company; potential value comes from behind-the-scenes manufacturing and integration relationships.

ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: A useful speculative test on whether AI accelerators or photonics need more reliability screening and wafer-level burn-in, with a very clear backlog-and-win verification path.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Small-cap test name whose exposure is buried across multiple end markets rather than labeled cleanly as AI infrastructure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify data-center customer exposure, project backlog, pricing cyclicality, commodity sensitivity, and whether AI campus builds are material to revenue.

Raceway, conduit, cable management, and related electrical products are not glamorous, but they may be necessary inputs in large campus builds and power-distribution projects.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify data-center and cloud infrastructure revenue mix, customer wins, backlog, margins, and whether AI hardware complexity improves economics.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify datacenter infrastructure revenue, rack or power manufacturing exposure, customer concentration, margin profile, backlog, working-capital changes, and whether AI demand is incremental rather than merely re-labeled existing business.

This is not yet proven from the supplied evidence, but it fits the Serenity lens better than obvious mega-cap demand names because the exposure may be hidden inside broad EMS and infrastructure segments. The candidate is testable through segment disclosures, datacenter customer commentary, backlog, margin mix, working-capital behavior, and AI-specific program references.

Customer confidentiality can obscure whether Flex is participating in high-value rack, power, cooling, or integrated system programs.

ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Facility and safety services are several steps away from AI capex headlines and may not be explicitly labeled as data-center exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify cloud/datacenter customer programs, exact hardware category exposure, whether AI-related programs are incremental, customer concentration, operating margins, inventory build, and cash-conversion behavior.

The reason to keep it near the top is not evidence strength but testability: if AI infrastructure programs are material, they should eventually appear in cloud/customer commentary, segment growth, margins, capex, inventory, or backlog. It is slightly behind Flex because the supplied candidate context gives less specific linkage to power and rack manufacturing.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Jabil is usually viewed as a diversified EMS and manufacturing-services company, not as a pure AI infrastructure bottleneck. Any AI relevance may be embedded inside broad customer programs rather than visible as a named product line.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Track AI cluster networking revenue, Ethernet adoption, optical attach rates, customer concentration, supply constraints in related optical components, and whether AI networking growth is broadening beyond the most visible cloud customers.

Inference: AI cluster networking demand is durable and Arista can help validate the downstream pull-through into Ethernet switching, optics, DSPs, transceivers, and network architecture. However, its mega-cap status, high attention, and relatively obvious AI networking exposure reduce mispricing and underfollowed-discovery scores.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether there is any material AI infrastructure, robotics, edge inference, industrial automation, datacenter management, or embedded-control exposure; otherwise remove from later layers.

ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Speculation: Raspberry Pi Holdings may have some relevance to edge AI, robotics, industrial automation, embedded computing, or developer ecosystems, but the supplied evidence does not establish material AI infrastructure exposure. It remains in the list only as a shadow hypothesis because it is obscure relative to the main datacenter AI buildout and could be one or two steps away from obvious demand drivers.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is not typically framed as an AI datacenter infrastructure supplier. If there is relevance, it would likely be indirect through edge inference, industrial automation, robotics prototyping, or embedded control rather than hyperscale AI clusters.
